notes: The refresh button re-lists snapshots. Measured as a RATE on the CANOPY SERVER LOG, not on browser requests -- the list fetch is issued server-side from the Dash callback, so zero browser GETs is EXPECTED and browser-side counting reads as 'never refreshes' (a first pass recorded exactly that and was the wrong instrument). Idle baseline: 7 'Fetching snapshots from API' lines in 60 s = 2.33 per 20 s. Driven: 4 clicks inside a 20 s window produced 4 fetches -- a clean 1:1 above baseline (exceeds_idle_baseline true). A single 3 s window after one click is NOT sufficient here: idle gaps range 4-29 s, so one window cannot separate signal from the interval's own jitter.

Declared value verified in source: DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 10000 (juniper-canopy/src/frontend/components/hdf5_snapshots_panel.py:53), with the JUNIPER_CANOPY_SNAPSHOTS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS override at :84 and the fallback at :89/:91. Observed live on two independent STRICTLY IDLE 60 s windows: 5 fetches (median gap 8.77 s) and 7 fetches (~8.6 s apparent period) -- both bracketing the declared 10 s once the documented F-CANOPY-004 callback jitter is allowed for. Idle matters: an earlier measurement taken while the driver was clicking produced gaps from 0.33 s to 92 s, all self-inflicted. Recorded as consistent-with-10 s rather than as an exact period.

The View Details button writes the snapshot id into -selected-id by parsing its pattern id. Proved on the _dash-update-component WIRE, which was necessary: a DOM-only reading said the detail never rendered and would have been a wrong FAIL. Responses observed in order: {'hdf5-snapshots-panel-selected-id': {'data': null}} then {'hdf5-snapshots-panel-selected-id': {'data': 'snapshot_20260813T051936Z'}}, followed by a request for detail-panel.children carrying that id as its input value. The leading null is F-CANOPY-009's clearing behaviour observed directly rather than inferred.

GET /api/v1/snapshots/{id} -> detail render. The panel populated with 'ID: snapshot_20260813T051936Z Name: snapshot_20260813T051936Z.h5 Timestamp: 2026-08-17 10:06...', replacing the 'Select a snapshot from the table above to view its details.' prompt. Sampling must be fast and tolerant: F-CANOPY-009 means the store is cleared and re-set around the click, so a window landing in the cleared half reads as 'never filled'.

The restore op button opens the shared confirm modal with a restore body, observed at 750 ms: 'Confirm Restore of snapshot:snapshot_20260813T051936Z / Load this snapshot for inspection and modification. Training is NOT started — invoke Retrain or Resume to begin a training run.' Opening is RACY (see the note on M-SNAPSHOTS-13) and required re-querying the button id immediately before the click.

The replay op button opens the same modal with a replay body, observed at 900 ms (visible 900 ms before self-close): 'Confirm Replay of snapshot:snapshot_20260813T051936Z / Start a read-only playback session of this snapshot's training histo...'.

The resume op button opens the same modal with a resume body, observed at 900 ms (visible 600 ms): 'Confirm Resume of snapshot:snapshot_20260813T051936Z / Continue training from where this snapshot left off. The pre-resume ...'.

The retrain op button opens the same modal with a retrain body, observed at 1200 ms (visible 1500-2400 ms across runs): 'Confirm Retrain of snapshot:snapshot_20260813T051936Z / Use this snapshot's weights and topology as a starting point for a ...'.

The modal body carries all THREE documented parts, captured untruncated (the driver's probe helper slices textContent to 120 chars and was cutting the third off -- a reading artifact, not a missing line): 'Confirm Restore of snapshot:snapshot_20260813T051936Z' + the op description + '⚠️ Training must be paused or stopped before any snapshot operation.' (248 chars total). IMPORTANT RACE NOTE, and a finding NOT filed because of it: the modal open fails intermittently and the failing op VARIES between runs -- restore+replay failed one pass while resume+retrain succeeded, then restore succeeded and resume failed on the next. The wire shows the cause is F-CANOPY-010's early-out, whose response is {'restore-modal': {'is_open': false}, 'restore-modal-body': {'children': ''}, 'restore-pending-id': ...} i.e. the documented (False, '', None). It is NOT op-specific; a two-attempt 'restore never opens' reproduction looked convincing and was wrong.

Cancel closes the modal and issues NO request. Modal opened at 750 ms, cancel clicked, modal gone 300 ms later, and the POST hook recorded posts_seen: [] -- no /api/v1/snapshots POST of any kind. -restore-status stayed empty, as it must for a cancelled op.

Confirm issues POST /api/v1/snapshots/{id}/{op} and the 200 path renders ✅ into -restore-status. Triple-confirmed, because the canopy POST is server-side (zero browser posts is expected, never a failure): (1) UI -- '✅ Restored from snapshot 'snapshot_20260813T051936Z''; (2) backend FSM moved STOPPED -> INVESTIGATING; (3) GET /v1/network went from no/empty network to hidden_units: 10, i.e. the snapshot's 10-unit topology genuinely rehydrated. Confirm must be clicked the instant the body appears (done at 600 ms) because F-CANOPY-010 discards the pending op id ~3.6 s later. active_tab correctly stayed 'Snapshots' -- only replay switches it (M-SNAPSHOTS-16). Observation, not a new finding: monitor.current_hidden_units still read 0 while /v1/network read 10 -- the stale-counter class already covered by F-CANOPY-006.

A confirmed REPLAY additionally switches the active tab -- the row's distinguishing claim vs M-SNAPSHOTS-15. Observed: modal opened at 1000 ms (attempt 3 of 4, the F-CANOPY-010 race), confirm clicked immediately, -restore-status rendered '✅ Snapshot replay started', and the active tab moved 'Snapshots' -> 'Replay' with replay-player-panel present. This is the third visualization-tabs.active_tab writer the matrix names (D-1).

The history toggle opens -history-collapse and loads GET /api/v1/snapshots/history into -history-content. Collapse opened at 1200 ms (attempt 2 -- same rebuild race) and the content rendered real records: '📸 CREATE snapshot_20260813T051936Z 2026-08-13 05:19:36 Snapshot created successfully • REPLAY_STOPPED snapshot_20260811T010849Z ... • REPLAY snapshot_20260811T010849Z ... Started replay o...'. The independent API read (GET /api/v1/snapshots/history -> 200) returns the same action records, so the panel is rendering real backend history rather than a placeholder.

-dataset-swaps-content renders from dataset-swap-events-store and, with no swap events recorded, correctly shows its empty state: 'No dataset swaps recorded yet.'
